name: Zurich
tagline: Global Finance Hub, Lakeside Living, and the World's Highest Prices
description: Zurich pairs a global financial center with lake-and-Alps quality of life and public services that top international rankings, with Mercer placing it first in the world for quality of living in 2024. It is consistently among the two or three most expensive cities on earth, so the appeal is stability, safety, world-class healthcare, and near-flawless infrastructure rather than cost arbitrage. Everyday costs, from groceries and dining to transit and mandatory health insurance, sit well above even London or Paris. German is the working language, though English is widely spoken across the finance sector.

quickFacts.visa: No dedicated retirement visa. EU/EFTA citizens settle by proving sufficient means and holding Swiss health insurance. A non-EU retiree depends on the discretionary Art. 28 FNIA permit (age 55 or over, sufficient means, and genuine personal ties to Switzerland), granted canton by canton. Zurich abolished lump-sum taxation in 2009, so the wealthy-foreigner tax route used in some cantons is closed here. US, UK, Canadian and Australian visitors get 90 Schengen days in any 180. Compulsory KVG health insurance within 3 months of arrival, and a C permit follows after about 10 years, 5 for US and Canadian citizens.
quickFacts.language: German (Swiss German spoken, standard German written); English widely spoken in business
quickFacts.internetSpeed: Gigabit fiber widely available; city median around 400-600 Mbps (~CHF 45-80/mo)
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very safe; low violent crime, with petty theft mainly around the main station and nightlife areas
quickFacts.climate: Temperate continental with warm summers and cold winters, moderated by Lake Zurich

housing.description: Small studio in an outer district such as Schwamendingen, Seebach, or Altstetten, the cheapest rents in the city

dining.description: Mostly home cooking, with the occasional inexpensive lunch or takeaway

healthcare.description: Mandatory KVG basic insurance only, Region 1, CHF 1,000 franchise on a managed-care model

transportation.description: A ZVV two-zone travelcard covering trams, buses, and S-Bahn, no car

entertainment.description: A gym or occasional cinema, with free lakeside and hiking days doing the rest

1M.lifestyle: A frugal but genuinely comfortable footing in one of the world's priciest cities. A small studio in an outer district, a ZVV pass that reaches the whole city and lake, and the mandatory KVG cover everyone here carries. Most meals are cooked at home, with an inexpensive lunch out now and then. The compensation is a setting where the lake, the forests, and the tram network are effectively free and minutes away. Little slack for travel, but hard to beat at this price.

housing.description: A modest one-bedroom outside the centre in Oerlikon or Altstetten

dining.description: Eating out twice a week or so, plus the odd nicer dinner

healthcare.description: KVG standard model, CHF 500 franchise, with light complementary and dental cover

transportation.description: A ZVV two-zone monthly pass plus occasional regional trips

entertainment.description: Gym, cinema, and a modest events budget

2M.lifestyle: An unshowy, secure footing. A modest one-bedroom outside the centre, eating out twice a week or so, and a fuller health plan than the bare minimum. The pass covers daily movement, and a gym and cinema round out the week. This is the practical middle of the city, comfortable without stretching, with the lake and trams always close.

housing.description: A central, desirable one-bedroom in Kreis 4/5, Wiedikon, or lower Enge

dining.description: A regular mix of casual spots and mid-range restaurants through the week

healthcare.description: KVG basic insurance on a standard model plus outpatient and dental supplementary (VVG) cover

transportation.description: A broader-zone ZVV pass with occasional taxi or ride-hail, still no car

entertainment.description: Concerts, theatre, weekend day-trips, and ski days in season

3M.lifestyle: The comfortable, unhurried version of the city. A central one-bedroom within walking distance of the lake and nightlife, dining out through the week, and a real cultural calendar of concerts, theatre, and winter ski days. Supplementary health cover sits on top of the mandatory plan, and the pass plus the occasional taxi cover everything without a car. There is genuine monthly margin for travel and spontaneity. This is a comfortable retirement in a city that tops the quality-of-life rankings.

housing.description: A spacious high-standard central one-bedroom or small two-bedroom in a prime quarter such as Enge or Seefeld

dining.description: Frequent dining at nicer restaurants, wine included

healthcare.description: KVG plus semi-private hospital (VVG) cover with two-bed rooms and free doctor choice

transportation.description: The ZVV pass with regular taxis and Mobility car-share

entertainment.description: Theatre and opera, a ski-season budget, and premium events

domesticHelp.description: A cleaner around four hours a week

luxuryExtras.description: A season ski pass, wellness and spa, and premium memberships

5M.lifestyle: An affluent, low-friction life. A spacious high-standard flat in a prime lakeside quarter, frequent dining at the city's better tables, and semi-private health cover that removes waiting. A weekly cleaner keeps the home, taxis and car-share supplement the pass, and there is a standing budget for theatre, spa, and ski weekends. Upscale living with the lake and mountains at hand, comfortably short of the top tier's ceiling.

housing.description: A luxury furnished two- to three-bedroom at a prime address such as the Zurichberg, the Seefeld lakeside, or the Gold Coast edge

dining.description: Fine dining on demand, from lakeside institutions to the city's best tables

healthcare.description: KVG basic insurance plus top private worldwide hospital cover with free choice of specialist

transportation.description: An owned or leased car with prime central parking, plus taxis

entertainment.description: Opera and concert subscriptions, ski chalets, private clubs, and a full leisure calendar

luxuryExtras.description: Concierge services, private-club memberships, and an uncapped travel and lifestyle budget

10M.lifestyle: The top of what the city offers short of buying property. A furnished luxury home on the Zurichberg or the Seefeld lakeshore, dining anywhere without a second thought, and top private healthcare with free choice of specialist. A car with prime parking joins the trams, near-daily household help keeps the home, and the discretionary budget funds opera subscriptions, ski chalets, private clubs, and constant travel. The city absorbs large budgets easily, and this tier uses that headroom.
